code:
.text
.globl main

main:
    # print user prompt string
    li $v0, 4
    la $a0, input
    syscall    

guess:
    # read integer - will be copied to v0
    li $v0, 5
    syscall

    # our secret number is 7!
    li $s0, 7

    # if v0 == our secret number s0
    beq $s0, $v0, correct

    # incorrect code
    li $v0, 4
    la $a0, wrong
    syscall       

    # loop until the user gets it right
    j guess

correct:
    li $v0, 4
    la $a0, right
    syscall       

exit:
    # exit
    li $v0, 10
    syscall  

.data
    input: .asciiz "Can you guess my secret number between 1 and 10?  Enter it below\n"
    wrong: .asciiz "Not quite!\n"
    right: .asciiz "You guessed it!\n"
description: Use a backward jump (j guess) and a conditional branch (beq) to repeat the integer-reading block until the guess equals 7.

steps.description: In `main`, print the initial `input` prompt string once using syscall 4.

At `guess:`, read an integer with syscall 5 into `$v0` and load `7` into `$s0`. Branch to `correct` if `$s0 == $v0`. Otherwise print `wrong` (`"Not quite!\n"`) and jump back to `guess` with `j guess`.
When `beq` branches to `correct:`, print `right` (`"You guessed it!\n"`) and fall through to `exit:` to terminate with syscall 10.
Notice how placing the `guess:` label before syscall 5 and `j guess` after printing `wrong` turns the conditional check into a loop that repeats until `$v0` equals `$s0`.

steps.answer: Jumping back to line 10 reads a new guess with syscall 5 without re-printing the initial `input` prompt string on lines 6-8.
steps.question: Why is the `guess:` label placed at line 10 instead of line 4 (`main:`)?

steps.description: `beq $s0, $v0, correct` compares `$s0` (7) against `$v0`; when they differ, execution continues to line 22.
After printing `Not quite!`, `j guess` jumps back to line 10 to read the next guess.

title: Repeating a Guess Loop with Labels and Jumps in MIPS
